title: Understanding Mean Square Error
text: Mean Square Error (MSE) is a way to measure how close a predicted value is to the actual value. It is calculated by taking the average of the squares of the differences between predicted and actual values. Can you think of how this might apply to our problem?

title: Calculating MSE
text: To calculate the MSE, you need to find the difference between each predicted value and the actual value, square those differences, and then find the average of those squared differences. What would be the first step in this process?

title: First Step in MSE Calculation
text: What is the difference between the first predicted value and the actual value?

title: Squaring the Differences
text: Once you have the differences between the predicted and actual values, the next step is to square each of these differences. Why do you think squaring is necessary?

title: Squaring the First Difference
text: What is the square of the difference you calculated in the previous step?

title: Averaging the Squared Differences
text: After squaring all the differences, the final step is to find the average of these squared differences. How would you calculate this average?
